newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices fall on increased supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices fall on increased supply.

text.p: Cotton prices fell on Wednesday on increased arrivals and sluggish demand from mills, dealers said. They said sentiment was subdued in the absence of any fresh release for export quota by government.
In spot deals, Bengal-deshi fell 10 rupees to 820/850 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned lost 20 rupees to 1,400/1,630 rupees per maund, dealers said.

New crop arrivals in the Punjab region rose to 28,000/30,000 bales (170 kg each) against 25,000 bales reported on Tuesday, they said. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) remained steady at 17,800/18,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
